idiom_name: MassTransit IConsumer<TCommand> over a command record; System.Text.Json discriminator on the wire
implementation_notes: The dominant .NET realization is a messaging framework rather than hand-written plumbing: a command is a record or class (SubmitOrder, ReserveStock), IBus.Send publishes it, and MassTransit routes it to the single IConsumer<TCommand> implementation while deriving broker topology from the message types - the point-to-point contract, the handler registry and the retry/dead-letter policy are framework machinery, not application code. On the payload side System.Text.Json supplies the wire discriminator for polymorphic hierarchies through [JsonPolymorphic]/[JsonDerivedType] with a $type property (.NET 7+), which replaces a hand-written type tag. Hand-rolled command envelopes appear only when a raw broker client is used instead, or when the wire format must match another platform exactly.
pitfalls: A command is meant to have exactly one consumer: registering a second IConsumer<TCommand> silently turns the command channel into competing consumers of the same work.
System.Text.Json requires the $type discriminator to be the first property of the JSON object; messages produced by other platforms need AllowOutOfOrderMetadataProperties or a custom converter.
A polymorphic base type without [JsonDerivedType] round-trips as the base type, so derived command properties are silently dropped when the payload is deserialized.
